why: This file pins the herdr wire vocabulary — method names, result discriminators, error codes, agent status words, both event-kind spellings, subscription types and their pane scoping, agent kinds, and the metadata source id and state-label keys — as one machine-checked contract that three audiences are diffed against:

the live server, via internal/herd/wirevocab's drift test that runs `herdr api schema --json` whenever a herdr binary is on PATH; the client, whose Go constants are pinned member-for-member by internal/herd/client/vocabulary_contract_test.go; and the herdtest fake, which is validated (constants, served replies, and a live dial of every builtin) by internal/herd/herdtest/vocabulary_test.go.

The vocabulary drifts silently otherwise. herdr ships a schema but the client speaks hand-typed constants and the fake hand-writes its replies; a rename on either side is invisible until a run fails far from the cause. Every category that the live schema enumerates is compared for SET EQUALITY in both directions, so a server-side addition fails this test too, deliberately: extensibility means the counts grow, and the failure is the alarm that the client surface may want the new word. Bump this file consciously.

The file follows the shape of contracts/collect-vocabulary.json (why prose up top, then one object per diffable category) but lives here, not there: contracts/ is a digest-pinned vendored bundle from pengelbrecht/ticks whose file set `contracts check` freezes on every go test — adding to it breaks the build by design.

Snapshot taken against herdr 0.9.0 (advertises protocol 22) on 2026-09-10. The client still pins protocol 20 / herdr 0.8.2; the 0.8.2→0.9.0 vocabulary change was additive, and the client's constants are a strict subset of this contract, so a pinned-20 client runs against a 0.9.0 server unchanged.

Two spellings of the same event world exist and both are pinned: the underscored `event` schema (kind repeated in a data `type` field) and the dotted `subscription_event` schema. herdr reuses the DOTTED subscription name verbatim as the subscription_event kind, and the three dotted kinds are exactly the three pane-scoped subscription types — the loader enforces both rules.

Error codes are NOT enumerated by the schema (error_response's code is an open string), so that category cannot be live-diffed; its members are the observed set, each with provenance in `notes`, and the offline checks pin the client's constants and the fake's vocabulary to it.

Agent kinds are not in the schema either; the 23 members are the `[possible values: ...]` list of `herdr agent start --help`, and the drift test re-reads that help text. This repo's .tick/runners.toml uses only pi, codex and claude; no Go code pins kinds as constants, so the category carries no client_used annotation.
`ok` is a real result discriminator, not an absence of one: both report_metadata methods answer a bare `{"type":"ok"}` and echo no pane or workspace object.
This repo has no herdr plugin yet; when one exists, pin its events.on names here as a new category.
Every schema-enumerated category below was extracted verbatim from the live schema dump, and the drift test re-extracts with the same paths, so the provenance matters more than usual:

methods from schemas.request.oneOf[].properties.method.const; result discriminators from schemas.success_response.$defs.ResponseResult.oneOf[].properties.type.const; underscored event kinds from schemas.event.$defs.EventKind.enum; dotted subscription-event kinds from schemas.subscription_event.$defs.SubscriptionEventKind.enum; subscription types and their pane-scoping (the variants whose `required` names pane_id) from schemas.request.$defs.Subscription.oneOf.
observations: 2026-09-10: herdr 0.9.0 at ~/.local/bin/herdr; `herdr api schema --json` answers with no server running (verified via env -i), so the drift test needs no live session and is cheap enough for every test run.

2026-09-10: schema protocol 22, schema_version 1; 102 methods, 64 result discriminators, 26 underscored + 3 dotted event kinds, 27 subscription types (3 pane-scoped), 5 agent statuses, 4 pane agent states, 23 agent kinds from the CLI help.
error_response.code is an open string in the schema — error codes can only be observed, never diffed.
state_labels keys are unrestricted in the schema, but herdr's rendering rule is one label per agent status, so the contract pins the key set to agent_statuses and the loader enforces the equality.

report_metadata tokens: propertyNames pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$, maxProperties 16; ttl_ms bounds 1 to 86400000 — one millisecond to one day, and zero is not a value (no expiry is expressed by OMITTING ttl_ms, which a painter should not want).

why: Every method name the request schema accepts. The client speaks an 18-constant subset (client_used) and the herdtest fake mirrors 17 of those 18 — it has neither a constant nor a builtin for pane.wait_for_output — so a single list keeps the three honest against each other.
Every `result.type` value the success_response schema can carry. `ok` is a real member of this set, not a placeholder: the report_metadata methods answer with it and nothing else.

The schema cannot enumerate error codes (the code field is an open string), so this is the observed set with per-member provenance in `notes`. The set is open-ended by design: an unrecognised code is an opaque server error, not a contract violation — the drift test therefore does not diff this category.
Two members have no Go constant yet (agent_not_ready, unsupported_event_wait_match); they are pinned here so that a future constant lands in the same vocabulary, not beside it.

notes.agent_not_found: The agent target does not resolve. Client constant CodeAgentNotFound.
notes.agent_not_ready: Prompting an agent whose launch is still pending (agent.start answered launch_pending). Documented in herdtest's Config.LaunchPending and internal/herd/spawn's readiness gate: sample agent.get until readiness flips. Observed against herdr 0.8.x; no Go constant yet.
notes.agent_pane_busy: agent.start's target pane is not at an available shell prompt — notably in the first few hundred ms of a worktree.create'd pane. Transient startup race, not a rejection. Client constant CodeAgentPaneBusy.
notes.agent_prompt_stalled: agent.prompt observed no state change after submitting: herdr's own detection of the dropped first prompt. Transient; the documented recovery is to send it again. Client constant CodeAgentPromptStalled.
notes.invalid_request: The envelope or params failed to parse; also what herdtest answers for an unexpected method. Client constant CodeInvalidRequest.
notes.pane_not_found: The pane id does not resolve. Client constant CodePaneNotFound.
notes.timeout: A waiting method's (agent.wait, events.wait, pane.wait_for_output) deadline elapsed. Client constant CodeTimeout.
notes.unsupported_event_wait_match: events.wait with a match other than pane agent-status — herdr 0.8.0 only implements status matches. Documented in internal/herd/client/events.go; no Go constant yet.
notes.workspace_not_found: The workspace id does not resolve. Client constant CodeWorkspaceNotFound.

why: The underscored kinds of the `event` schema: EventsWait results and every session-wide subscription. The client defines a constant for each (client_used == members), and its accessors additionally accept the dotted spellings of the three pane-scoped subscriptions below.

The dotted kinds of the `subscription_event` schema. Exactly the three pane-scoped subscription types, spelled like the subscription that asked for them — the loader and the drift test both enforce the equality with subscription_types.pane_scoped.

The dotted names an events.subscribe request may carry. The three pane_scoped members require a pane_id; every other one is session-wide and silently ignores a stray pane_id on the wire, which is why the client validates scoping before dialling and why the contract pins the scoping alongside the names.
AgentStatus as the request schema enumerates it. The client pins all five, and herdr's metadata state-label keys are exactly these words (see metadata.state_label_keys_are).
PaneAgentState as the subscription_event schema enumerates it. NOT the same set as agent_statuses: there is no `done` pane state — a pane never reports completion, only the agent on it does.

The kind values `herdr agent start --help` lists. Not in the schema, so the drift test reads the help text instead. Deliberately without client_used: no Go code pins kinds, and the manifest is expected to grow — a new kind failing the drift test is the alarm to bump this list, nothing more.
This repo's .tick/runners.toml uses only pi, codex and claude.
The output slices pane.read and subscriptions can select.
The output encodings pane.read can return.
The match kinds pane.wait_for_output and the output-matched subscription accept.
The sounds notification.show can ask herdr to play.
Where herdr may render an in-app toast for notification.show.

The metadata channel's own vocabulary. source_id is OUR source id, not the server's — herdr keys expiry and overwrite on the source string, so it is load-bearing and pinned here and against the client's SourceHerdPaint constant.

state_label_keys_are names the category whose members the state-label keys must equal, and state_label_keys spells them out: herdr renders one label per agent status, so the key set IS the status set. The loader enforces the equality against the named category, so a status added upstream surfaces here too.
The token and ttl pins mirror the schema's PaneReportMetadataParams (see source.observations); the drift test re-checks them against the live schema.
